page.overview:
What is Battle of the Department of Mysteries?

The Battle of the Department of Mysteries, also known as the Battle of the Ministry of Magic, was the very first major conflict of the Second Wizarding War. It took place on 18 June 1996, after the powerful Dark wizard Lord Voldemort secretly lured his archenemy Harry Potter to the Department of Mysteries inside the British Ministry of Magic in London in an effort to obtain the prophecy concerning his future defeat at Potter's hands, as the young wizard was the one prophesied to end Voldemort and his dark reign for good.

Once at the Ministry, Harry was cornered by at least a dozen Death Eaters, but the young hero was aided by five of his fellow members of Dumbledore's Army: Ron Weasley, Hermione Granger, Neville Longbottom, Ginny Weasley, and Luna Lovegood; all of whom managed to successfully hold their ground and fend off the Death Eaters until the Order of the Phoenix came to their rescue.

In the resulting skirmish, the prophecy was accidentally destroyed, Voldemort was personally seen by Minister Cornelius Fudge himself, all but one of the Death Eaters were captured by Albus Dumbledore, and Sirius Black was killed by his deranged and sadistic cousin Bellatrix Lestrange. In the immediate future the Ministry of Magic went to take proper action against Voldemort's newfound rising power, thus the start of open warfare.

In 1980, at the height of the First Wizarding War, which lasted for eleven years (from 1970 to 1981), Sybill Trelawney, the great-great-granddaughter of the famous seer and magical hypnotist Cassandra Trelawney, was being interviewed by Albus Dumbledore at the Hog's Head Inn in Hogsmeade for the position of Divination teacher at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. During the interview, Trelwaney suddenly entered into a heavy trance and predicted the future coming of the only person who could truly defeat and destroy Lord Voldemort, due to this particular wizard having strength, power, will, and most of all: a capability for love, that would not only equal and surpass those of the Dark Lord, but those of Albus Dumbledore himself. As a result, Dumbledore hired Trelawney in order to protect her from the Death Eaters.
